paragraphs: Leicestershire County Council has more than 700 children and young people in its care. It recruits and supports its own foster carers, and the independent agencies shown above also list Leicestershire among the areas they cover. Fostering with the county means caring for Leicestershire's own children alongside the social workers who plan for them; an agency assesses, trains and supervises its own carers and offers homes to councils when they need them.

The county's fostering service annual report for 2023-24 shows how stretched local homes are. It had 116 approved fostering households and was running at over 90% of its places in use, against a target of 75%, and it named large sibling groups and teenagers as the busiest area of referrals. The council's stated aim is for children to live in Leicestershire with Leicestershire carers wherever that is possible and right for them, and the report records that it made more use of its own carers compared with agencies that year.

To foster with the county you need to be over 21, with no upper age limit, and couples need to have lived together for at least 12 months. Relationship status and sexual orientation make no difference, you do not need to own your home, and health issues are looked at case by case rather than ruling you out. A child needs a spare room, although a baby can share yours and brothers and sisters can share, and you will need some relevant childcare experience.

There is more than one way in: short-term and longer-term fostering, specialist roles for children from about six (including parent and child care), bridging placements, respite for other carers, short breaks for children with medical or additional needs, and supported lodgings for young people aged 16 and over. Carers have a supporting social worker, a team available 365 days a year, local training and carer-run support groups.

Our Leicestershire allowance page sets out the council's 2026/27 payments: a weekly allowance from £182 for a child aged up to 4 to £267 for a young person of 16 or over, plus a skills fee on top. Every new carer starts at Level 1, which for one child comes to £227.50 to £333.75 a week, rising to £436.80 to £640.80 at Level 4. There is also a £374.70 set-up allowance and extra weeks for birthdays, festivals and holidays. Leicester city has its own council fostering service, so if you live in the city see the Leicester page. Near the county's edges, the Rutland, Northamptonshire, Warwickshire and Derbyshire pages may also help. Speak to the council and two or three of the services above before you choose.
